summary: This article explains how winds such as the Shamal and haboobs lift sand and dust across Arabia, how sandstorms affect people and nature, and how to stay safe.
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “Sandstorms of Arabia” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: a strong wind that blows across Saudi Arabia and the Gulf from the northwest
how far you can see clearly
a very small piece of something

challengeTerms.def: a substance that living things need in order to grow and stay healthy
a feature that helps a living thing survive in its environment
a dust storm pushed forward by the cold winds rushing out of a thunderstorm

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that sandstorms do more harm than good? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain two different ways sandstorms affect people and one way they affect nature.
struggling: Pre-teach Shamal, visibility, and particle with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses nutrient, adaptation, and haboob to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
